requirement.original: What ACTUALLY killed sessions in the last hour, causing watcher auto-restore?
requirement.clarified: Determine exact cause of session deaths at 09:05 UTC and whether the cascading restore amplified the damage
requirement.what: Root cause investigation of session deaths and cascading restore behavior
requirement.why: User experienced disruptive auto-restore that killed all sessions when only 1 died naturally
success_criteria: Single session death does not trigger kill-all-and-respawn cascade
Daemon restart scenario still properly cleans orphans
constraints: Must not break daemon-restart orphan cleanup

root_cause_analysis.symptom: Watcher auto-restored all 14 sessions at 09:05 when user only archived/lost 1 session
root_cause_analysis.root_cause: restore_online_sessions() kills ALL running session processes as 'orphans' before re-spawning, even when only 1 session died. Lines 889-907 of happy-session-recovery.sh.
root_cause_analysis.root_cause_commit: N/A - design flaw in restore logic, not a regression
root_cause_analysis.why_introduced: Orphan kill was designed for daemon-restart scenario where ALL old processes need replacement
root_cause_analysis.why_problematic: Same logic runs on single-session-death, killing 13 healthy sessions to restore 1 dead one
root_cause_analysis.timeline: Existing behavior, but became visible with 14+ sessions where cascade impact is severe

evidence.not_oom: dmesg empty, journalctl -k empty for oom/kill/memory
evidence.actual_trigger: Daemon log at 09:05:26: 'Removing stale session with PID 289607 (process no longer exists)' -- natural Claude process exit
evidence.cascade_proof: Recovery log shows 6 'Killed orphaned process' entries at 09:05:40-42 for sessions that were alive and healthy

context.recent_commits: N/A - script not in happy repo

file_contents.orphan_kill_logic: Lines 889-907: kills all running processes matching --resume for each home, then re-spawns all saved sessions
file_contents.scan_running_sessions: Lines 43-170: correctly identifies daemon-tracked vs orphan processes

cascade_pattern.trigger: 1 session process exits naturally (Claude SDK exit, context limit, etc.)
cascade_pattern.step2: Restore kills ALL running processes for the home as 'orphans'
cascade_pattern.step3: Re-spawns all sessions from session_dirs.txt (13-14 sessions)
cascade_pattern.step4: Some newly spawned sessions die during startup (resource contention)
cascade_pattern.step5: Watcher detects MORE deaths, triggers another restore (but 'already running' prevents second)
cascade_pattern.result: 1 death -> 14 kills -> 14 respawns -> 1-2 more deaths -> another full restore

development_approach.strategy: Modify restore logic to only kill+respawn sessions that are actually missing, not all sessions
development_approach.fix_direction: In restore_online_sessions(), compare running sessions against saved sessions. Only kill processes for UUIDs that need re-spawning. Skip kill for sessions that are already running and healthy.
development_approach.validation_approach: Manually kill a single Claude process and verify only that session is re-spawned while others remain untouched

research_findings.reason: Root cause investigation based on log analysis, not a design/architecture decision
